The MSM keeps occasionally bringing up this controversy; even Trump has chimed in on it. But it's not really valid on its face.

When USPS ships a package: They accept it at a post office nearby to the shipper, check it in, set its route, truck it several stops along its network to the office that handles the final delivery, and your local postman takes it to your house (or whatever).

For the packages that USPS offers a 50% discount to, Amazon routes the package along its own network to a facility relatively local to the recipient, then drops it off at that post office handling the actual delivery, with everything it drops off pre-sorted to quickly go where it needs to, requiring a lot less work from the USPS.

Were the USPS required to discontinue the discount, Amazon, if it still sent packages via USPS, would be shipping them in the normal fashion, dropping them off at a local post office. Amazon would no longer need the workers doing the transportation, and USPS would need new transportation workers. Unionized transportation workers. And therein lies the motive for raising the controversy.
tl;dr the "Amazon not paying USPS enough" controversy is actually a union labor dispute
